boards.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
boards.description: Ten food-focused destinations with currently published late or late-evening availability near UNC-Chapel Hill.

cards.title: Cosmic Cantina
cards.subtitle: 118 E Franklin St, Chapel Hill
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s pickup page to confirm service before heading out, especially after 2 a.m., when it asks customers to call first.
cards.short_summary: A Franklin Street burrito stop with the latest published hours in this set.
cards.evidence_claim: Cosmic Cantina’s official Chapel Hill page lists pickup and delivery hours of 11 a.m.–4 a.m. daily, with a request to call after 2 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists service until 4 a.m. daily and advises calling after 2 a.m. to confirm availability.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Knox Way
cards.subtitle: 48 Knox Way, Chapel Hill
cards.notes: This is a drive-thru-friendly option rather than a promise of late indoor seating; check the restaurant page for the day’s operating status.
cards.short_summary: A Chapel Hill chain location with nightly late drive-thru hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell’s official location page lists drive-thru hours from 9 a.m. to 2 a.m. every day at 48 Knox Way.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell in Chapel Hill, NC — 48 Knox Way
cards.access_notes: Official page lists drive-thru service until 2 a.m. daily; its listed dine-in hours end earlier, at 11 p.m.

cards.title: Wendy's on Scarlet Drive
cards.subtitle: 100 Scarlet Dr, Chapel Hill
cards.notes: Use the official location page to check restaurant or drive-thru availability before traveling south of the campus core for a late meal.
cards.short_summary: A Chapel Hill quick-service restaurant with 2 a.m. published closing times.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy’s official Chapel Hill location page lists restaurant and drive-thru hours until 2 a.m. every day.
cards.source_title: Wendy's at 100 Scarlet Dr. in Chapel Hill, NC
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists both restaurant and drive-thru service from 10 a.m. until 2 a.m. daily.

cards.title: Insomnia Cookies
cards.subtitle: East Franklin Street, Chapel Hill
cards.notes: Check the bakery’s dedicated Chapel Hill page before going or ordering; its page headline specifically advertises late daily delivery.
cards.short_summary: A cookie bakery with an official Chapel Hill ordering page promoting 3 a.m. delivery.
cards.evidence_claim: Insomnia Cookies’ official Chapel Hill store page is titled “Warm Cookies Delivered Until 3 AM Daily.”
cards.access_notes: The official Chapel Hill store page advertises warm-cookie delivery until 3 a.m. daily; verify pickup details directly before leaving.

cards.title: The Yogurt Pump
cards.subtitle: 106 W Franklin St, Chapel Hill
cards.notes: Check the flavor list and then plan a frozen-yogurt stop on West Franklin; Friday and Saturday have the latest published closing time.
cards.short_summary: A Franklin Street frozen-yogurt shop open into the late evening.
cards.evidence_claim: The Yogurt Pump’s official website lists hours until 10 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and 11 p.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists hours until 10 p.m. Sunday–Thursday and 11 p.m. Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Chase Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: South Campus, UNC-Chapel Hill
cards.notes: Check the current campus menu or schedule before walking over, since the documented late-night service applies Sunday through Thursday during term operations.
cards.short_summary: UNC’s south-campus dining hall with documented midnight late-night service.
cards.evidence_claim: The Daily Tar Heel reported in March 2026 that Chase Dining Hall offers late-night extended dining until midnight Sunday through Thursday.
cards.source_title: Students frustrated by limited dining hours | The Daily Tar Heel
cards.access_notes: Published March 2026 reporting documents late-night dining until midnight Sunday–Thursday; campus schedules can change during breaks.

cards.title: Papa Johns on West Franklin
cards.subtitle: 607B W Franklin St, Chapel Hill
cards.notes: For a late carryout order, check the official store page and note that its latest listed times fall on Friday and Saturday nights.
cards.short_summary: A West Franklin pizza location with weekend carryout extending past midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Papa Johns’ official Chapel Hill location page lists carryout until 1:40 a.m. Friday and Saturday, and delivery until 2 a.m. on those nights.
cards.source_title: Papa Johns Pizza in Chapel Hill, NC — W Franklin St
cards.access_notes: Official page lists Friday–Saturday carryout through 1:40 a.m. and delivery through 2 a.m.; other days close earlier.

cards.title: Wings Over Chapel Hill
cards.subtitle: 313 E Main St, Carrboro, near UNC
cards.notes: This Carrboro location is named for Chapel Hill; confirm pickup or delivery timing on its official page before making the trip from campus.
cards.short_summary: A nearby Carrboro chicken-wing restaurant open after midnight every night.
cards.evidence_claim: Wings Over’s official Chapel Hill location page lists hours until 1 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 2 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists hours until 1 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 2 a.m. Friday–Saturday; the physical location is in Carrboro.

cards.title: Mediterranean Deli
cards.subtitle: 410 W Franklin St, Chapel Hill
cards.notes: Use the deli’s official location page before a late-evening meal or pickup; it lists a single daily schedule for its Franklin Street restaurant.
cards.short_summary: A West Franklin restaurant with official service hours through 9 p.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Mediterranean Deli’s official website lists its Chapel Hill location at 410 W Franklin Street open daily from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Official website lists Chapel Hill service daily until 9 p.m.

cards.title: Al's Burger Shack
cards.subtitle: 516 W Franklin St, Chapel Hill
cards.notes: Treat this as an earlier late-evening dinner stop and verify the restaurant’s official locations page before setting out, especially around holidays.
cards.short_summary: A West Franklin burger restaurant with a published 9 p.m. closing time.
cards.evidence_claim: Al’s Burger Shack’s official locations page lists its Franklin Street Chapel Hill location open daily from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Official locations page lists the Franklin Street restaurant open daily until 9 p.m.

boards.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named UNC destinations for studying, gathering, art, science, and outdoor time, supported by current university and cultural-institution sources.

cards.title: Davis Library
cards.subtitle: Main campus library · study space
cards.notes: Start with the building directory, then choose a seat or reserve a study room when your work needs a shared table and fewer interruptions.
cards.short_summary: A large campus library with general study seating and reservable rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC identifies Davis Library as a campus library open to everyone and describes campus libraries as providing study spaces for different preferences.
cards.access_notes: Check University Libraries hours and room-reservation information before going.

cards.title: House Undergraduate Library
cards.subtitle: North Campus · study space
cards.notes: Use the House Undergraduate Library as a change-of-scene study stop; check its current hours before planning a longer session.
cards.short_summary: An undergraduate-focused library included among UNC’s welcoming campus libraries.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC lists the House Undergraduate Library among campus libraries open to everyone and states that the library system offers study spaces.
cards.access_notes: Confirm building hours and any access updates through University Libraries.

cards.title: Wilson Special Collections Library
cards.subtitle: North Campus · special collections
cards.notes: Pair a study visit with a look at current special-collections offerings, and ask staff about using collection materials for class research.
cards.short_summary: A special-collections library that is part of UNC’s campus library network.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC lists the Wilson Special Collections Library among campus libraries open to everyone and describes library spaces and research expertise.
cards.access_notes: Collection use and reading-room procedures may differ from general library spaces.

cards.title: Health Sciences Library
cards.subtitle: Health Sciences campus · study space
cards.notes: Use this library when health-related coursework needs a focused work setting; review current building hours and service details before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A named UNC campus library supporting study and research.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC lists the Health Sciences Library among campus libraries open to everyone and states that campus libraries provide study spaces and research expertise.
cards.access_notes: Check the Health Sciences Library’s current access and hours information.

cards.title: Kenan Science Library
cards.subtitle: Science campus · subject library
cards.notes: Bring science-course questions or reading here, then use the library’s listed services and spaces to structure a focused work block.
cards.short_summary: A subject-specific UNC library for science-oriented study and research.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC states that subject-specific branch libraries are open to everyone and that campus libraries offer study spaces and research expertise.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current Kenan Science Library schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Carolina Union
cards.subtitle: 209 South Road · student union
cards.notes: Meet a classmate, use the building map to orient yourself, or settle in to study, eat, or relax during posted Union hours.
cards.short_summary: UNC’s student union combines gathering space, services, student involvement, and events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Carolina Union invites visitors to study, eat, or relax there and provides programs, services, facilities, student-organization support, and reservable space.
cards.access_notes: The Union posts building hours; some services, food vendors, and reservable spaces have separate schedules or requirements.

cards.title: Coker Arboretum
cards.subtitle: Cameron Avenue and Raleigh Street · outdoor garden
cards.notes: Take the walking paths past trees and seasonal plantings, pause on an open lawn or bench, and avoid the arbor path while its renovation continues.
cards.short_summary: A five-acre UNC garden with walking paths, lawns, benches, and seasonal plant displays.
cards.evidence_claim: The North Carolina Botanical Garden describes Coker Arboretum as a five-acre UNC-campus garden with walking paths, lawns, benches, and dawn-to-dusk daily access.
cards.access_notes: Open dawn to dusk, 365 days a year. The arbor path along Cameron Avenue is closed for renovation, with reopening expected after July 2026 work.

cards.title: Forest Theater
cards.subtitle: Battle Park · outdoor performance venue
cards.notes: Walk through Battle Park to see the stone seating and natural bowl, then check event organizers before attending a scheduled performance or gathering.
cards.short_summary: An open-air UNC performance space with a long connection to Carolina Playmakers.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC A to Z identifies Forest Theater as an outdoor performance space in Battle Park that remains in use for performances and other gatherings.
cards.access_notes: Public events and venue use vary; follow event-specific entry and ticket instructions.

cards.title: Ackland Art Museum
cards.subtitle: 101 S. Columbia Street · campus-adjacent museum
cards.notes: Drop in to view the galleries, use the gallery map to pace your visit, and check the calendar for current programs or extended Second Friday hours.
cards.short_summary: UNC’s art museum offers free gallery admission near Franklin Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ackland Art Museum states that admission is always free and provides current visiting hours, gallery maps, exhibitions, and public programming.
cards.source_title: Visit the Ackland Art Museum at UNC-Chapel Hill
cards.access_notes: Admission is always free. Current hours are Wednesday–Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m., Sunday 1–5 p.m.; Second Friday is open until 9 p.m.

cards.title: Morehead Planetarium and Science Center
cards.subtitle: 250 E. Franklin Street · UNC-Chapel Hill
cards.notes: Check the day’s science programs and exhibits before you go, then allow time to navigate the UNC-owned parking lot or arrive by transit.
cards.short_summary: A campus science center with public programs and planetarium shows.
cards.evidence_claim: Morehead Planetarium and Science Center identifies its location on UNC-Chapel Hill’s campus, lists public hours, and publishes science programming and planetarium shows.
cards.access_notes: The center posts current hours and program schedules online; individual planetarium shows or events may have separate ticket requirements.

boards.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten named Chapel Hill places where students can spend time outdoors, see art, or use free UNC student admission without purchasing anything.

cards.title: Browse the Ackland galleries
cards.subtitle: 101 S. Columbia St, Chapel Hill
cards.notes: Meet inside the museum and move through the changing exhibitions at your own pace; check the posted gallery hours before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A free museum visit centered on changing exhibitions and collection displays.
cards.evidence_claim: Ackland Art Museum states that admission is free and lists public gallery hours.
cards.access_notes: Open Wed–Sat 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sun 1–5 p.m.; closed Mon–Tue and selected holidays.

cards.title: Explore Morehead’s exhibits
cards.subtitle: 250 E. Franklin St, Chapel Hill
cards.notes: Bring a valid UNC One Card to request free general admission, then explore the exhibits and Science LIVE! offerings included with it.
cards.short_summary: UNC students can enter Morehead’s exhibit areas without buying general admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Morehead says UNC-Chapel Hill students with a valid One Card receive free general admission, including all-day exhibit access.
cards.source_title: Plan a Visit — Morehead Planetarium and Science Center
cards.access_notes: Free general admission is for UNC students with a valid One Card; planetarium shows have a separate discounted charge.

cards.title: Sit with Exhale at 140 West
cards.subtitle: 140 W. Franklin St, Chapel Hill
cards.notes: Use the Town-owned plaza as a meet-up point, take in the Exhale artwork, or pause there while walking downtown.
cards.short_summary: A Town-owned downtown public plaza with a signature public artwork.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town identifies 140 West Plaza as a Town-owned and maintained open space with the Exhale art piece and community events.
cards.source_title: 140 West Franklin Plaza — Town of Chapel Hill
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public plaza; no admission or purchase is listed.

cards.title: Walk Pritchard Park’s trails
cards.subtitle: 100 Library Dr, Chapel Hill
cards.notes: Take the paved or natural-surface paths together and look for the outdoor art; pack only what you need for a dawn-to-dusk visit.
cards.short_summary: A 34-acre Town park with trails, outdoor art, and nature-play features.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town lists Pritchard Park’s trails, art, and other park features, with hours from dawn to dusk.
cards.source_title: Pritchard Park — Town of Chapel Hill
cards.access_notes: Outdoor park open dawn to dusk; use the trails and public features without reserving a facility.

cards.title: Take a lap on Fan Branch Trail
cards.subtitle: 100 Sumac Rd, Chapel Hill
cards.notes: Walk the fitness course along Fan Branch Trail or spread out on the open grass; avoid reservable fields and shelters for a no-cost visit.
cards.short_summary: A large Town park with a fitness course, trail, open grass, and picnic areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town lists Fan Branch Trail, a fitness course, open grass, and picnic areas among Southern Community Park’s features.
cards.source_title: Southern Community Park — Town of Chapel Hill
cards.access_notes: Outdoor park open dawn to dusk; do not use a reserved field, court, or shelter.

cards.title: Follow the forest hiking trail
cards.subtitle: 121 Collums Rd, Chapel Hill
cards.notes: Make a short, low-key trail loop through the wooded park, then use the public benches or picnic area before leaving by dusk.
cards.short_summary: A wooded neighborhood park with a forest hiking trail and outdoor recreation features.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town describes North Forest Hills Park as a wooded space with a forest hiking trail, benches, and outdoor facilities.
cards.source_title: North Forest Hills Park — Town of Chapel Hill
cards.access_notes: Outdoor park open dawn to dusk; trail use does not require a facility rental.

cards.title: Hang out beside Booker Creek
cards.subtitle: 600 Kensington Dr, Chapel Hill
cards.notes: Bring a friend to the seating and small grassy area, then take a quiet break beside the tree cover and Booker Creek edge.
cards.short_summary: A small neighborhood green space with seating, grass, and creekside tree cover.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town lists seating, a grassy outdoor-play area, tree cover, and Booker Creek at Coker Hills West Park.
cards.source_title: Coker Hills West Park — Town of Chapel Hill
cards.access_notes: Outdoor neighborhood park open dawn to dusk; use its public seating and grass area without reserving anything.

cards.title: Walk the Meadowmont wooded paths
cards.subtitle: 621 Meadowmont Ln, Chapel Hill
cards.notes: Circle the scenic pond and wooded walking trails, or use the picnic shelter only when it is not reserved for another group.
cards.short_summary: A Town park with a pond, wooded walking trails, and a no-charge picnic shelter.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town lists Meadowmont Park’s scenic pond and wooded walking trails; its fee schedule lists the Meadowmont Park shelter as no charge.
cards.source_title: Meadowmont Park — Town of Chapel Hill
cards.access_notes: Outdoor park open dawn to dusk. The Town fee schedule lists Meadowmont Park’s shelter as no charge; respect existing reservations.

cards.title: Stroll Ephesus Park’s wooded paths
cards.subtitle: 1501 Ephesus Church Rd, Chapel Hill
cards.notes: Use the wooded paths for a conversation walk and pause at the public benches; leave court rentals out of this zero-cost plan.
cards.short_summary: A Town park with quiet wooded paths and public outdoor space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town describes Ephesus Park as having quiet wooded paths and lists it as a community park open from dawn to 10 p.m.
cards.source_title: Ephesus Park — Town of Chapel Hill
cards.access_notes: Outdoor park open dawn to 10 p.m.; walking the paths does not require renting a court.

cards.title: Visit the Gene Strowd Rose Garden
cards.subtitle: Chapel Hill Community Center Park, 120 S. Estes Dr
cards.notes: Take a slow loop through the rose varieties and companion plants, then use the surrounding park trails for a longer outdoor hang.
cards.short_summary: A public rose garden inside Chapel Hill Community Center Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town’s recreation guide states that the Gene Strowd Community Rose Garden is free and open to the public daily.
cards.source_title: Winter–Spring 2026 Recreation Guide — Town of Chapel Hill
cards.access_notes: The Town states the garden is free and open to the public daily; it is within Chapel Hill Community Center Park.

boards.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For

cards.title: Davis Library Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Davis Library
cards.notes: Open the library’s room-reservation page before heading over, then choose a room that fits your group’s work and planned session.
cards.short_summary: Reservable study rooms in UNC’s largest campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Libraries provides a dedicated reservation page for Davis Library study rooms.
cards.source_title: Davis Library Study Rooms | UNC Libraries
cards.access_notes: Use the official reservation page to review current room availability and any booking requirements.

cards.title: House Undergraduate Library Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: House Undergraduate Library
cards.notes: Use the official space scheduler to check the room list and select an available setup before bringing a partner or project group.
cards.short_summary: Bookable rooms within the undergraduate-focused library.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Libraries’ space-reservation system lists rooms for the House Undergraduate Library.
cards.source_title: House Undergraduate Library Spaces | UNC Libraries
cards.access_notes: Check the official scheduler for current availability, capacity, and reservation rules.

cards.title: Health Sciences Library Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: Health Sciences Library
cards.notes: Check the Health Sciences Library space calendar for a room or setting that matches your task, especially when you need a defined workspace.
cards.short_summary: Library study options on UNC’s health-sciences campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC Libraries maintains a reservable-spaces listing for the Health Sciences Library.
cards.source_title: Health Sciences Library Spaces | UNC Libraries
cards.access_notes: Review the official space listing for current room details, availability, and access conditions.

cards.title: Wiggle Room Cubicles
cards.subtitle: Manning Hall
cards.notes: Reserve a Wiggle Room through the School of Information and Library Science calendar when you need a bounded setting for a call or meeting.
cards.short_summary: Reservable cubicles in Manning Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC SILS provides an official reservation page for Wiggle Rooms in Manning Hall.
cards.source_title: Wiggle Rooms | UNC School of Information and Library Science
cards.access_notes: Consult the official SILS calendar for current reservation availability and applicable use rules.

cards.title: Computer Science Experience Labs
cards.subtitle: Sitterson Hall
cards.notes: Check the CSXL site before arriving and use its current information to determine whether the lab environment fits your computing work.
cards.short_summary: A computing-centered academic space in Sitterson Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Computer Science Experience Labs are a UNC computer science facility.
cards.source_title: Computer Science Experience Labs | UNC Computer Science
cards.access_notes: Consult the CSXL website for current access, operating information, and any user eligibility requirements.

cards.title: Wilson Special Collections Library
cards.subtitle: South Campus
cards.notes: Plan a focused reading session around Wilson’s collections, and confirm current visitor guidance before relying on the building for your work.
cards.short_summary: A special-collections library listed among UNC’s campus libraries.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC identifies Wilson Special Collections Library as one of its campus libraries and states everyone is welcome in campus libraries.
cards.source_title: Resources: Academic and Research | UNC–Chapel Hill
cards.access_notes: Check UNC Libraries’ current location information before visiting, as collection and reading-room access may have separate procedures.

cards.title: Kenan Science Library
cards.subtitle: UNC–Chapel Hill campus
cards.notes: Use this subject-library setting when science materials support the work at hand, and confirm current location details before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A named subject library in UNC’s campus library system.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC states that its campus library system includes subject-specific branch libraries and offers study spaces for different preferences.
cards.source_title: Resources: Academic and Research | UNC–Chapel Hill
cards.access_notes: Verify current library access and hours through UNC Libraries before arrival.

cards.title: Music Library
cards.subtitle: UNC–Chapel Hill campus
cards.notes: Bring music-related reading or listening work here, then check the library’s current location and service information before you go.
cards.short_summary: A subject-library setting for music-focused academic work.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC states that its campus library system includes subject-specific branch libraries and study spaces.
cards.source_title: Resources: Academic and Research | UNC–Chapel Hill
cards.access_notes: Confirm current access and services through UNC Libraries before planning a visit.

cards.title: UNC Library Makerspace
cards.subtitle: UNC Libraries
cards.notes: Use the makerspace when a project benefits from making or prototyping; review available equipment and current policies before planning your session.
cards.short_summary: A library workspace for 3D scanning and printing projects.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC describes its Library makerspace as offering 3D scanning and printing.
cards.source_title: Resources: Academic and Research | UNC–Chapel Hill
cards.access_notes: Review current makerspace equipment, training, and access requirements through UNC Libraries before use.

cards.title: Media and Design Center
cards.subtitle: UNC Libraries
cards.notes: Bring a multimedia assignment from concept into production here, and check equipment and staff-support guidance before scheduling your work.
cards.short_summary: A library production environment for multimedia projects.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC says the Media and Design Center provides production equipment, technology, digital assets, and staff expertise for multimedia projects.
cards.source_title: Resources: Academic and Research | UNC–Chapel Hill
cards.access_notes: Confirm current Media and Design Center access, equipment availability, and any booking requirements before visiting.

boards.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten documented destinations on Franklin Street and its immediately adjacent downtown corridors, each with a specific reason to stop.

cards.title: Ackland Art Museum
cards.subtitle: South Columbia Street, beside West Franklin Street
cards.notes: Enter from South Columbia Street and use the gallery map to choose an exhibition or collection area before you start looking around.
cards.short_summary: A free UNC art museum steps south of Franklin Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ackland Art Museum is at 101 S. Columbia Street near West Franklin Street, and admission is always free.
cards.access_notes: Open Wed–Sat and Sun; confirm holiday closures and current gallery access before going.

cards.title: Morehead Planetarium and Science Center
cards.subtitle: East Franklin Street corridor
cards.notes: Check the day’s planetarium-show listings, then allow time to explore the science-center offerings around your scheduled program.
cards.short_summary: A UNC science center at 250 E. Franklin Street with planetarium programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Morehead Planetarium and Science Center is located at 250 E. Franklin Street on UNC-Chapel Hill’s campus and lists planetarium shows.
cards.access_notes: Programs and ticket requirements vary; consult the current event listing before arrival.

cards.entity_name: Joan H. Gillings ArtSpace at CURRENT
cards.title: Joan H. Gillings ArtSpace at CURRENT
cards.subtitle: West Franklin Street corridor
cards.notes: Look at Carolina Performing Arts’ calendar first and plan around a listed performance, installation, or event at the Franklin Street venue.
cards.short_summary: Carolina Performing Arts’ immersive and interdisciplinary-art hub on Franklin Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Joan H. Gillings ArtSpace at CURRENT and CURRENT Studio are at 123 W. Franklin Street and serve as Carolina Performing Arts’ hub for immersive and interdisciplinary art.
cards.access_notes: Dates, times, and admission depend on the individual performance or event.

cards.title: Varsity Theatre
cards.subtitle: East Franklin Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the theatre’s current schedule to select a film and verify its rating and start time before heading to 123 East Franklin.
cards.short_summary: A movie theatre at 123 E. Franklin Street with a current public schedule.
cards.evidence_claim: Varsity Theatre’s schedule lists film showtimes, and the Town identifies the theatre at 123 E. Franklin Street.
cards.access_notes: Showtimes and film ratings change; confirm the current schedule and age appropriateness before purchasing.

cards.title: Epilogue Books Chocolate Brews
cards.subtitle: East Franklin Street corridor
cards.notes: Browse the independent-bookstore shelves, then check the venue calendar for an all-ages-appropriate reading, conversation, or music event.
cards.short_summary: An independent bookstore and chocolatería at 109 E. Franklin Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Epilogue Books Chocolate Brews is an independent bookstore and Spanish-style chocolatería at 109 E. Franklin Street.
cards.access_notes: Retail and food purchases are optional; review event details for any age or ticket requirements.

cards.title: Carolina Coffee Shop
cards.subtitle: East Franklin Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the Franklin Street address to find the storefront, then choose from the posted food, coffee, and tea offerings during service hours.
cards.short_summary: A sit-down restaurant and café at 138 E. Franklin Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Carolina Coffee Shop is at 138 E. Franklin Street and offers food along with coffee and tea.
cards.source_title: Coffee Shops in Chapel Hill and Orange County
cards.access_notes: A purchase is required for food or drinks; verify current hours directly with the business.

cards.title: Sutton's Drug Store
cards.subtitle: East Franklin Street corridor
cards.notes: Stop at the 159 East Franklin storefront to see the historic site, then review the current menu and service details before ordering.
cards.short_summary: A long-running Franklin Street restaurant documented at 159 E. Franklin Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Chapel Hill Historical Society identifies Sutton’s at 159 E. Franklin Street; the official tourism authority describes it as a Chapel Hill tradition since 1923.
cards.access_notes: Food purchases are optional; check current operating information before visiting.

cards.title: Peace & Justice Plaza
cards.subtitle: East Franklin Street corridor
cards.notes: Pause at 179 East Franklin Street to read the site context, then continue along the downtown corridor with its civil-rights history in view.
cards.short_summary: A downtown plaza connected to Chapel Hill civil-rights movements.
cards.evidence_claim: Peace & Justice Plaza at 179 E. Franklin Street is identified as a site of civil-rights movements beginning in the 1960s.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public-space access may be affected by scheduled events or temporary Town operations.

cards.title: Greetings from Chapel Hill mural
cards.subtitle: Rosemary Street, immediately behind West Franklin Street
cards.notes: Walk around to the Rosemary Street side behind He’s Not Here and photograph the mural from the public right-of-way without blocking access.
cards.short_summary: A 1941-postcard-inspired mural on the Rosemary Street side of West Franklin.
cards.evidence_claim: The “Greetings from Chapel Hill” mural is on the back side of He’s Not Here at 112½ W. Franklin Street, along Rosemary Street.
cards.source_title: 17 Must-See Murals in Chapel Hill and Orange County
cards.access_notes: View from public areas and respect adjacent businesses and private-property boundaries.

cards.title: Chapel Hill/Orange County Welcome Center
cards.subtitle: West Franklin Street corridor
cards.notes: Pick up a downtown walking map or ask staff for current public information before continuing along Franklin Street and nearby corridors.
cards.short_summary: The county tourism authority’s information center at 308 W. Franklin Street.
cards.evidence_claim: The Chapel Hill/Orange County Visitors Bureau Welcome Center is located at 308 W. Franklin Street and lists public visitor hours.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Mon–Fri 8:30 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sat 10 a.m.–3 p.m.; confirm before visiting.

boards.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Carolina rituals, annual gatherings and campus customs.

cards.title: Start Classes With First Sip
cards.subtitle: Old Well, McCorkle Place
cards.notes: On the first day of classes, visit the Old Well and take part in First Sip if the fountain is operating; use the accessible approach and respect the queue.
cards.short_summary: A first-day water ritual connected with luck and the hope of a perfect GPA.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC identifies First Sip as the tradition of students drinking Old Well water for good luck and a perfect GPA on the first day of classes.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; fountain availability and campus conditions can change.

cards.title: Find the Tree That “Holds Up” Carolina
cards.subtitle: Davie Poplar, McCorkle Place
cards.notes: Pause at Davie Poplar to learn the campus legend linking the tree’s fate to the University; view it from established paths and do not touch or climb it.
cards.short_summary: A centuries-old campus myth attached to Carolina’s historic tulip poplar.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC documents the legend that the University will fall if Davie Poplar falls, while noting the myth’s origin is unknown.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor historic tree in McCorkle Place; keep off protected landscaping.

cards.title: Listen for the Student Bell Ringers
cards.subtitle: Morehead-Patterson Bell Tower
cards.notes: Listen from public campus space on a football game day or special occasion, when student master bell ringers operate the Bell Tower.
cards.short_summary: Students carry forward a bell-ringing tradition at Carolina’s signature tower.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC says student master bell ringers oversee Bell Tower operations and ring its bells on football game days and other special occasions.
cards.access_notes: Ringing is event-dependent; do not seek access to the tower’s controlled interior.

cards.title: Plan for the Senior Bell Tower Climb
cards.subtitle: Morehead-Patterson Bell Tower
cards.notes: Eligible graduating Tar Heels can watch for official Senior Week details for this Bell Tower climb; do not attempt entry outside authorized access.
cards.short_summary: A graduation-season opportunity to climb one of Carolina’s defining landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC states that graduating Tar Heels have the opportunity to participate in the Senior Bell Tower Climb.
cards.access_notes: Participation is limited to official opportunities; follow Alumni Association instructions.

cards.title: Look for the Live Rameses
cards.subtitle: Carolina athletic events
cards.notes: At an authorized athletics event, look for Rameses and enjoy the live-mascot tradition from the audience area; follow staff instructions around the animal.
cards.short_summary: Carolina’s live ram mascot tradition began at a 1924 football game.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC states that the live animal Rameses mascot began attending Carolina football games in 1924.
cards.access_notes: Appearances are event-dependent and may require an event ticket.

cards.title: Spot the Costumed Rameses
cards.subtitle: Carolina athletic events
cards.notes: Watch for the costumed Rameses at a Carolina event and enjoy from public spectator space; mascot appearances vary by sport and schedule.
cards.short_summary: A student-carried mascot role that began with the 1987–88 basketball season.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC says the costumed Rameses tradition began when Eric Chilton first wore the costume for the 1987–88 basketball season and continues today.
cards.access_notes: Appearances are event-dependent and venue admission rules may apply.

cards.title: Make Space for Arts Everywhere Day
cards.subtitle: UNC-Chapel Hill campus
cards.notes: Check the annual program and join an activity that fits your interests, from singing and dancing to painting; follow each host’s participation guidance.
cards.short_summary: A campuswide annual arts celebration held since 2017.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC states that Tar Heels have celebrated the annual Arts Everywhere Day tradition since 2017, with activities including singing, dancing and painting.
cards.access_notes: Annual programming, locations and any registration requirements vary.

cards.title: Join the Colors at Holi Moli
cards.subtitle: UNC-Chapel Hill campus
cards.notes: Attend through the official event organizers, wear clothes suitable for color powder and follow on-site guidance about accessibility, cleanup and participation.
cards.short_summary: A yearly campus celebration of Holi that brings students and the local community together.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC says Holi Moli has been a yearly Carolina tradition since 2008 and connects campus with the local community.
cards.access_notes: Annual event details and participation instructions are set by the organizers.

cards.title: Mark Carolina’s University Day
cards.subtitle: Memorial Hall, UNC-Chapel Hill
cards.notes: Watch for the annual Oct. 12 ceremony and attend only with current event information; it commemorates Old East’s cornerstone and honors members of the Carolina community.
cards.short_summary: Carolina’s annual ceremony marking the founding-era cornerstone of Old East.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC states that University Day marks the Oct. 12, 1793 laying of Old East’s cornerstone, was first celebrated in 1877 and includes annual recognition of distinguished alumni.
cards.access_notes: The annual ceremony’s venue, entry policies and schedule should be confirmed on the current event page.

cards.title: Sing “Hark the Sound”
cards.subtitle: University programs and athletic events
cards.notes: Learn the alma mater before an event, then join in when invited; Carolina identifies it as a song sung at University programs and sporting events.
cards.short_summary: The alma mater that closes many Carolina gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC’s family handbook identifies “Hark the Sound” as the alma mater and says it is sung at University programs and sporting events.
cards.source_title: Carolina Family Handbook | UNC New Student and Family Programs
cards.access_notes: Occurs in event contexts; attendance and accessibility conditions depend on the hosting program.

warnings: Several traditions are event- or eligibility-dependent; confirm current University scheduling and access guidance before going.

boards.school_name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A daylight-first sequence through named campus landmarks, a museum, and a science center; confirm current hours and event availability before setting out.

cards.title: Start with the UNC Visitors Center
cards.subtitle: Morehead Building · campus orientation stop
cards.notes: Pick up the self-guided historic-campus context here, then use it to set a walking route before exploring the nearby landmarks.
cards.short_summary: Begin with campus context and a route.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC’s visitor guide identifies the Visitors’ Center in the Morehead Building and describes recorded historic-campus tours.
cards.access_notes: Check the Visitors Center’s current tour and office availability before arrival.

cards.title: Pause at the Unsung Founders Memorial
cards.subtitle: Historic campus · memorial stop
cards.notes: Read the memorial’s interpretation and take a moment to recognize the enslaved and free people of color it honors before continuing.
cards.short_summary: A reflective stop in the historic-campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC’s visitor guide says the Class of 2002 memorial honors enslaved and free men and women of color who helped build Carolina.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor memorial; follow any posted campus access guidance.

cards.title: Find the Caldwell Monument
cards.subtitle: Historic campus · landmark stop
cards.notes: Use the visitor-guide route to locate the white marble obelisk and connect it with Joseph Caldwell’s role as the University’s first president.
cards.short_summary: A named monument on the historic-campus route.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC’s visitor guide identifies the Caldwell Monument as a white marble obelisk at the burial site of first president Joseph Caldwell.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; visit during normal campus access periods.

cards.title: Continue to Davie Poplar
cards.subtitle: Historic campus · tree landmark
cards.notes: Stop beneath the named poplar and read the site in the context of the University’s founding story described in the visitor guide.
cards.short_summary: A historic tree landmark in the campus core.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC’s visitor guide describes the legend that William Richardson Davie rested under this tree when selecting the University site.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; stay on surrounding paths and respect any preservation barriers.

cards.title: See the Old Well
cards.subtitle: Historic campus · university symbol
cards.notes: Make this a short photo and orientation stop, then follow the brick walks toward Old East and the rest of the historic-campus route.
cards.short_summary: The University’s visual symbol and former water source.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC’s visitor guide calls the Old Well an unofficial University symbol and says it was one of the University’s few water sources for more than a century.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; follow posted guidance around the structure.

cards.title: Walk past Old East
cards.subtitle: Historic campus · residence hall
cards.notes: View the exterior and note its 1793 cornerstone; keep the stop outdoors because the building remains a residence hall.
cards.short_summary: A National Historic Landmark and active residence hall.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC’s visitor guide identifies Old East as a National Historic Landmark, says its cornerstone was laid October 12, 1793, and notes it is now a residence hall.
cards.access_notes: View from public outdoor areas; do not enter residential access areas.

cards.title: Pass South Building
cards.subtitle: Historic campus · administrative landmark
cards.notes: Take in the exterior and use the guide’s note about James K. Polk to add another chapter to the historic-campus walk.
cards.short_summary: A former dormitory that now houses University leadership offices.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC’s visitor guide says South Building was originally a dormitory, housed James K. Polk, and now contains the chancellor’s and other administrative offices.
cards.access_notes: View from public outdoor areas; office access may be restricted.

cards.title: Stop at Gerrard Hall
cards.subtitle: Historic campus · 1837 hall
cards.notes: Circle the building from the public walkways and use the visitor guide to place it among the long-running campus gathering spaces.
cards.short_summary: A named 1837 hall on the historic route.
cards.evidence_claim: UNC’s visitor guide states that Gerrard Hall was completed in 1837 and has been the scene of many University occasions.
cards.access_notes: Check University event scheduling before planning an interior visit.

cards.title: Spend an afternoon at the Ackland
cards.subtitle: 101 S. Columbia Street · art museum
cards.notes: Browse the galleries at your own pace, then check the current calendar for public art activities that fit the day you visit.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum with free public admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ackland states that admission is always free and lists its location at 101 S. Columbia Street in Chapel Hill.
cards.source_title: Visit the Ackland Art Museum at UNC-Chapel Hill
cards.access_notes: Regular hours listed are Wednesday–Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday 1–5 p.m.; verify holiday changes.

cards.title: Close with Morehead’s exhibits or a show
cards.subtitle: Morehead Building · science-center stop
cards.notes: Choose either general-admission exhibits or a scheduled planetarium show, and reserve or buy tickets only after checking the current calendar.
cards.short_summary: A ticketed planetarium option with UNC-student admission benefits.
cards.evidence_claim: Morehead lists Tuesday–Friday, Saturday, and Sunday hours and says UNC students with a valid One Card receive free general admission and $6 show bundles.
cards.source_title: Plan A Visit - Morehead Planetarium and Science Center
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Tue–Fri 10 a.m.–4:30 p.m., Sat 10 a.m.–6 p.m., and Sun 1–6 p.m.; ticketing applies to shows.
